nrIncident.routes: Various routes across the Chiltern Railways network
nrIncident.message:
The RMT union have announced industrial action that will impact Chiltern Railways today, Thursday 12 November.
The vast majority of services will be unaffected, with 90% of services expected to operate as scheduled. Most will experience a near normal train service.
Chiltern Railways will also be running their usual enhanced train service to and from Wembley Stadium to support the England vs Croatia football match in the evening. If you are travelling to this fixture, you should plan your journey as normal.
A visual disruption map video is available.
Please take note of the following impact:
• There are no Chiltern Railways services running between Leamington Spa and Stratford-upon-Avon all day. You should use West Midlands Railway services via Dorridge, with tickets being accepted at no extra cost
• There will be a small reduction in the overall number of Chiltern Railways services running between Leamington Spa and Birmingham Moor Street due to the local 'shuttle' services not running. If you are travelling to or from Hatton or Lapworth, you will be particularly affected
• There are no Chiltern Railways services north of Birmingham Moor Street all day. You should use West Midlands Railway services between Birmingham Moor Street and Stourbridge Junction, with tickets being accepted at no extra cost (please be aware that the last northbound service towards Stourbridge Junction, and onwards to Worcester Shrub Hill, departs Birmingham Moor Street at 22:57)
Additional information:
You can find more information on Chiltern Railways' dedicated Industrial Action page. This includes an extensive list of FAQs.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.
Compensation:
You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.

nrIncident.summary: Disruption to Southern services between Fareham and Cosham expected until the end of the day on Saturday 14 November
nrIncident.routes: Southern between Southampton Central and Brighton
nrIncident.message:
A points failure between Fareham and Cosham means fewer trains are able to run between these stations. As a result, trains running between these stations may be cancelled or diverted.
Disruption is expected until the end of the day on Saturday 14 November.
Customer advice:
Today on Friday 13th of November and tomorrow Saturday 14th of November trains that normally run between Brighton and Southampton will now run between Brighton and Bognor Regis.
This means that you may have to change more times than normal.
Please allow at least an additional 20 minutes to complete your journey.
Speak to station staff, look at the information boards or check your journey planner for the most recent information
How do I get from Brighton towards Southampton Central?
You will need to take a Southern service to Barnham. At Barnham change for a train towards Portsmouth. Change again at Fratton or Portsmouth & Southsea for a South Western Railway or Great Western Railway train direct to Southampton Central.
Please ensure to allow an additional 20 minutes to complete your journey and check journey planners and live departures before travelling.
How do I get from Southampton Central towards Brighton?
Take a train towards Portsmouth and change at Fratton or Portsmouth & Southsea. If there’s a direct train to Brighton, take that service. Otherwise, take a train that calls at Barnham and change there for Brighton.
Please ensure to allow an additional 20 minutes to complete your journey and check journey planners and live departures before travelling.
Can I use my ticket with another operator?
You can travel on the following services at no additional cost;
• Alternative Southern services between Brighton, Bognor Regis and Portsmouth Harbour
• South Western Railway services between Portsmouth Harbour and Southampton Central
• Great Western Railway services between Portsmouth Harbour and Southampton Central
Please be aware that using alternative travel will add at least 20 minutes to your journey depending on the route.
Planning your journey:
For help planning your journey, check live departure boards, view a live network map or see alternative route guides.
If you’re travelling within London, you can use the TfL Journey Planner.

Can you tell me more about the incident?
A points failure has been reported near Cosham, preventing trains from travelling on this route.
Points are movable sections of track that allow trains to change routes at junctions. If they develop a fault, they may not move into the correct position or the signalling system may be unable to confirm they are securely positioned. Sometimes, points can be secured in one position to allow some trains to continue. In this case, the points can be secured in a position that allows trains to use one route over the junction.
Network Rail signalling specialists are investigating the fault and working to restore services. Repairs may involve removing an obstruction, fixing the equipment or replacing faulty parts.
This disruption is expected to be impacting services until the end of Saturday the 14th of November
Ticket flexibility:
If your train is cancelled, you will be able to travel on an alternative service operated by any other participating train company, either two hours before or two hours after the original departure time of the cancelled service, in order to reach your destination.
If you decide not to travel or cannot complete your journey due to cancellations, you are entitled to a full refund from your original point of sale.
For further information and guidance please contact your train company or speak to a member of railway staff.
Check before you travel:
You can check your journey using the National Rail real-time Journey Planner.

You may be entitled to compensation if you experience a delay in completing your journey today. Please keep your train ticket and make a note of your journey, as both will be required to support any claim.

Customer advice:

Please check customer information boards and check online journey planners for the latest travel information.
Planning your journey:

Can you tell me more about the incident?
Track circuits are part of the signalling system and are used to detect where trains are on the railway. If one fails, the signalling system may show that a section of track is occupied even when there isn’t a train there. This means signals protecting that section will remain at red and trains cannot proceed normally.
Trains may still be able to run, but drivers will need to stop before the affected section and request verbal permission from the signaller before continuing past the red signal. They must then travel at a reduced speed so they can stop safely should they see anything ahead of them.
This takes longer than usual and can cause trains to queue behind one another. In severe cases, services may need to be cancelled, revised or diverted to prevent delays from building up across the wider network.
Network Rail signalling specialists are investigating the fault and will work to repair the affected equipment. Once the fault has been fixed and the signalling system is working normally, trains will be able to run at normal speeds again and the scheduled service can begin to recover.

Can you tell me more about the incident?
Track circuits are part of the signalling system and are used to detect where trains are on the railway. If one fails, the signalling system may show that a section of track is occupied even when there isn’t a train there. This means signals protecting that section will remain at red and trains cannot proceed normally.
Trains may still be able to run, but drivers will need to stop before the affected section and request verbal permission from the signaller before continuing past the red signal. They must then travel at a reduced speed so they can stop safely should they see anything ahead of them.
This takes longer than usual and can cause trains to queue behind one another. In severe cases, services may need to be cancelled, revised or diverted to prevent delays from building up across the wider network.
Network Rail signalling specialists are investigating the fault and will work to repair the affected equipment. Once the fault has been fixed and the signalling system is working normally, trains will be able to run at normal speeds again and the scheduled service can begin to recover.
